## Q95
Match List-I with List-II.

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. LRU | I. A page is written to secondary memory only when it has been selected for replacement |
| B. Demand cleaning | II. A page that has not been referenced for the longest time is replaced |
| C. Long term scheduling | III. The decision to add to the number of processes that are partially or fully in main memory |
| D. Medium term scheduling | IV. The decision to add to the pool of processes to be executed |

## Q95 - Options
(A) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
(B) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
(C) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
(D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

## Q95 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Memory Management, Page Replacement & Thrashing
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2023 (7 Dec, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q95

The correct match is **(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)**:

- **(A) LRU (Least Recently Used) matches (II):** A virtual memory page replacement algorithm that evicts the page that has not been referenced for the longest period of time, leveraging temporal locality.
- **(B) Demand cleaning matches (I):** In virtual memory cleaning policies, demand cleaning specifies that a modified (dirty) page is written to secondary storage only when it has been selected for replacement.
- **(C) Long term scheduling matches (IV):** The long-term (or job) scheduler determines which programs are admitted into the system from the job pool to become active processes, controlling the degree of multiprogramming.
- **(D) Medium term scheduling matches (III):** Medium-term scheduling is part of the swapping mechanism, deciding when to remove or bring back processes that are partially or fully in main memory to balance memory load.
